title: How an Airplane Wing Works in 60 Seconds ✈️🌬️ #shorts
description:
A jumbo jet can weigh over 400 tonnes, and its wings carry all of it. A curved, slightly tilted wing lowers the air pressure above it and throws air downward, and the air pushes back up. Flaps make the wing bigger for slow takeoffs and landings. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#airplane #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A jumbo jet can weigh over *400 tonnes*. Its wings hold all of that up in the air.

steps.label: Shape
steps.text: A wing is curved on top and tilted slightly into the wind. That tilt is the *angle of attack*.

steps.label: Pressure
steps.text: Air rushing over the top speeds up, and its *pressure drops*. Underneath, the pressure stays higher.

steps.label: Downwash
steps.text: The wing also bends the air *downward*. Push air down, and the air pushes the wing up.

steps.label: Lift
steps.text: Together that makes *lift*. Fly faster or tilt a little more, and you get even more of it.

steps.label: Flaps
steps.text: For slow takeoffs and landings, *flaps* slide out the back, making the wing bigger and more curved.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Curve, tilt, *lift*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
